questions.q: What composition principle was applied in the Bauhaus Dessau layout?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: Three wings spin off a central hub like a pinwheel, balanced without being mirrored.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the ziggurat?
questions.ref: General references on Mesopotamian architecture; Ziggurat of Ur (Ur-Nammu)
questions.n: It served the city's moon god. Pyramids are tombs; ziggurats are stairways to a shrine. Word root: Akkadian ziqqurratu, 'temple tower', from zaqaru, 'to build high'.

questions.q: Who assumes civil liability for the architectural plans, specifications, and contract documents he or she signed and sealed?
questions.ref: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR, definitions of Architect-of-Record, AICC, Consulting Architect, Foreign Architect
questions.n: Signing and sealing means accepting liability for that work.

questions.q: Which system grows plants without soil, using only water with dissolved nutrients?
questions.ref: UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); urban-agriculture terminology
questions.n: Word root: Greek hydor (water) + ponos (labor), so 'water-working'. Roots sit in water; no fish involved.

questions.q: Which Roman structure was dedicated to the gods?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on ancient Roman building types
questions.n: Word root: Latin templum, a space marked off as sacred. Thermae were public baths (Greek thermos = hot).

questions.q: Which architect is directly responsible for construction supervision of a project?
questions.ref: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR, definitions of Architect-of-Record, AICC, Consulting Architect, Foreign Architect
questions.n: AOR = design on paper; AICC = design on site.

questions.q: Which tropical design element is used in the tower's facade?
questions.ref: Public project descriptions by Arthaland, GFP Architects, and the IFC EDGE / World GBC case study
questions.n: Vertical fins sit between two glass layers to cut heat and glare. Think of them as the tower's sun-blocking eyelashes.

questions.q: Which architect is engaged for recognized expertise in a particular branch of architecture?
questions.ref: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR, definitions of Architect-of-Record, AICC, Consulting Architect, Foreign Architect
questions.n: A consultant is the specialist you call in, like a heritage or acoustics specialist. The recall list shortened this role to 'PCA'.

questions.q: Which part is the main hall used for living, dining, and sleeping?
questions.ref: Diksyonaryong Biswal term list cited in the supplied recall; common Filipino vernacular-architecture usage
questions.n: The bulwagan is the big shared room, the 'hall'. Silid is a separate small room. Think of the bulwagan as a studio apartment's main space.

questions.q: Fallingwater belongs to which architectural idea?
questions.ref: General references on Frank Lloyd Wright's life and works
questions.n: Organic means building and nature grow together. Fallingwater sits over a waterfall like a tree growing from the rock.

questions.q: Which Roman structure was used for public gatherings, courts, and civic business?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on ancient Roman building types
questions.n: Word root: Greek basilike stoa, 'royal portico'. Think of a town hall.

questions.q: Which permeable, outward-projecting platform or rack is used to hold and dry kitchen utensils?
questions.ref: Diksyonaryong Biswal term list cited in the supplied recall; common Filipino vernacular-architecture usage
questions.n: The banggerahan is a slatted rack that sticks out so water drips off. Dungawan means window (from dungaw, to peek out). Think of it as a built-in dish rack.

questions.q: What is the project construction cost (PCC)?
questions.ref: UAP Doc 202 (Design Services), schedule of minimum basic fees and payment phases
questions.n: PCC = area x cost per sq m. Think of it as the building's price tag before fees.

questions.q: Which strategy helps balance preservation and modernization?
questions.ref: General heritage-conservation practice (Intramuros / Casa Manila context)
questions.n: Keep the shell, give it a new job. Like turning an old train station into a museum.

questions.q: What is the RBF for architectural services only?
questions.ref: UAP Doc 202 (Design Services), schedule of minimum basic fees and payment phases
questions.n: Architectural-only = 60% of the A&E fee. A quick trick: multiples of 0.6 help you eliminate wrong choices fast. If your exam used the 6% table instead, the answer would be P1,710,000.

questions.q: Panic doors with lever handles that need little force illustrate which principle?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: A lever works with an elbow; a knob needs a grip. Less strength needed means more people can use it.

questions.q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum size of an accessible toilet cubicle?
questions.ref: 2024 Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344, NCDA/DPWH
questions.n: The older IRR used 1.70 x 1.80 m; the 2024 revision enlarged it to a square 1.80 m. 1.80 m is also the wheelchair turning space.

questions.q: Which Roman structure was the open city center and marketplace?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on ancient Roman building types
questions.n: The forum was the city's open living room. Word root: Latin forum, an open public place (related to foris, outside).

questions.q: Which architect is responsible for the plans and specifications and signs and seals them?
questions.ref: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR, definitions of Architect-of-Record, AICC, Consulting Architect, Foreign Architect
questions.n: AOR owns the design documents. Think of the AOR as the author whose name is on the book.

questions.q: For architectural-only services, what percentage of the RBF should the architect have received after completing schematic design and design development?
questions.ref: UAP Doc 202 (Design Services), schedule of minimum basic fees and payment phases
questions.n: Cumulative payments: 5% on signing, plus 10% at schematic design (15%), plus 20% at design development (35%). Some textbooks print slightly different phase splits, so confirm against your reviewer.

questions.q: Failure to provide or install safety measures for workers, inspectors, visitors, neighbors, and pedestrians is which class of violation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Surprising but true: it is listed under light violations in the IRR.

questions.q: What is the typical arch of Romanesque architecture?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on Romanesque architecture
questions.n: Romanesque uses the round, semicircular arch inherited from Rome. Word root: Roman + -esque (Italian -esco, 'in the manner of'), so 'Roman-like'. Memory trick: Romanesque = rainbow arch (round); Gothic = praying-hands arch (pointed).

questions.q: Which FLW work, built over a waterfall, is often called one of America's greatest buildings?
questions.ref: General references on Frank Lloyd Wright's life and works
questions.n: The Guggenheim is a spiral museum, not a waterfall house.

questions.q: What does retrofitting an existing building mean?
o: Adding or upgrading systems and performance after the building was built
questions.ref: General heritage-conservation practice (Intramuros / Casa Manila context)
questions.n: Word root: Latin retro (backward) + fit. 'Fitting in later', like adding a seat belt to an old car.

questions.q: How many main stairways lead up the Ziggurat of Ur?
questions.ref: General references on Mesopotamian architecture; Ziggurat of Ur (Ur-Nammu)
questions.n: Three staircases meet at a gateway on the first terrace. Think of a three-lane road merging into one gate.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height of a habitable room with natural ventilation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rules VII-VIII (light and ventilation)
questions.n: Natural ventilation needs more height so warm air rises above people. Word root: ventilare, Latin 'to fan', from ventus (wind).

questions.q: The client increases the floor area by 390 sq m. What is the new RBF for architectural services only?
questions.ref: UAP Doc 202 (Design Services), schedule of minimum basic fees and payment phases
questions.n: The new PCC passes P50M, so the first P50M is charged at 7% and the excess at 6%, then 60% is taken for architectural-only.

questions.q: Changing the existing use or occupancy without a Certificate of Change of Occupancy/Use/Operation is which class of violation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Changing use changes fire and life-safety demands, so it ranks highest. Grave = P10,000 fine.

questions.q: How many principles of universal design are there?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: The 7: equitable use, flexibility, simple and intuitive, perceptible information, tolerance for error, low physical effort, size and space for approach and use.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear ceiling height for a mezzanine?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rules VII-VIII (light and ventilation)
questions.n: Word root: Italian mezzano, 'middle', a half-floor between floors. It is the lowest ceiling in the set.

questions.q: A specification that requires compliance with ASTM, PNS, or similar published standards is called what?
questions.ref: Standard construction-specification practice (CSI-style spec types)
questions.n: It borrows a published rulebook instead of listing every detail.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height of a habitable room with artificial ventilation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rules VII-VIII (light and ventilation)
questions.n: A fan or aircon does the airflow work, so the room can be lower. Natural 2.70, artificial 2.40.

questions.q: What kind of walls are typical of Romanesque buildings?
o: Thin walls braced by flying buttresses
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on Romanesque architecture
questions.n: Mass is the structure. The walls themselves hold the weight, unlike Gothic where ribs and buttresses do the work.

questions.q: A single accessible entrance used by all users is an example of which principle?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: Word root: Latin aequus, 'level, equal'. One door for everyone, no separate side door.

questions.q: What do you call Wright's custom-designed concrete blocks reinforced with steel rods?
questions.ref: General references on Frank Lloyd Wright's life and works
questions.n: Patterned blocks are knitted together with rods like threads in fabric. Word root: textile = 'woven', from Latin texere.

questions.q: Failure to post the Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation is which class of violation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Posting is a paperwork-visibility issue, not a danger. Light = P5,000 fine.

questions.q: Which color palette best describes the Dessau building's exterior?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: White walls, dark steel frames, and grey tones. Primary colors belong to Bauhaus graphics and interiors, not the building's exterior.

questions.q: For vent shafts, what minimum cross-sectional area is required for every meter of shaft height?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rules VII-VIII (light and ventilation)
questions.n: Rule: 0.10 sq m per meter of height, but never less than 1.00 sq m, and least dimension not less than 600 mm. Taller shaft, bigger chimney.

questions.q: Romanesque architecture is most commonly described as a blend of which earlier traditions?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on Romanesque architecture
questions.n: Byzantine (from Byzantium) added domes and rich decoration to Roman arches and vaults. Gothic and Baroque came after Romanesque, so they cannot be ingredients of it.

questions.q: A specification that states exact materials, composition, and installation method is called what?
questions.ref: Standard construction-specification practice (CSI-style spec types)
questions.n: Prescriptive = 'written beforehand', like a recipe with exact ingredients and steps.

questions.q: Under the IRR fine schedule, what are the fines for light, less grave, and grave violations?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Fines climb in steps of seriousness.

questions.q: Which principle uses color contrast, tactile, and audible cues so information reaches users with any sensory ability?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: If you cannot see it, you can hear or feel it. Examples: tactile paving, audible elevator signals.

questions.q: Which element expresses 'transparency' in the workshop wing of the Bauhaus Dessau?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: The curtain wall hangs on the structure like a window-curtain, so the glass can run corner to corner.

questions.q: Which window head shape is characteristic of Romanesque buildings?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on Romanesque architecture
questions.n: Window heads echo the main arch: round for Romanesque, pointed for Gothic.

questions.q: What roof type does the Bauhaus Dessau building have?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: Flat roofs are a signature of Modernism.

questions.q: What is a primary challenge of retrofitting heritage buildings?
o: Modern codes do not apply to old buildings
No skilled workers exist at all
Heritage buildings can never be reused
Inserting new utility systems into old structures
questions.ref: General heritage-conservation practice (Intramuros / Casa Manila context)
questions.n: New ducts, pipes, and wires must fit without damaging old walls. Think of adding a modern kitchen to a grandmother's antique cabinet without cutting it.

questions.q: What is the detailed written document that defines the quality, materials, workmanship, and procedures of a project?
questions.ref: Standard construction-specification practice (CSI-style spec types)
questions.n: Drawings show what and where; specifications say how good and how built.

questions.q: Besides LEED Platinum and BERDE 5-star, which other green rating did the tower achieve?
questions.ref: Public project descriptions by Arthaland, GFP Architects, and the IFC EDGE / World GBC case study
questions.n: It was the world's first EDGE Zero Carbon building. EDGE = Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (IFC).

questions.q: Railings and a zocalo (kick base) that reduce falls and accidents illustrate which principle?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: Design assumes people slip, so it softens the mistake. Word root: zocalo comes from Italian zoccolo, 'little shoe', the base of a wall.

questions.q: Why are the floors of the bulwagan and batalan made of bamboo slats with small gaps?
o: For ventilation and to let spills and dust pass through
questions.ref: Diksyonaryong Biswal term list cited in the supplied recall; common Filipino vernacular-architecture usage
questions.n: Gaps let air rise from the silong and let water and dirt fall through. Think of the floor as a giant kitchen strainer: air and liquids pass, people stay on top.

questions.q: What is the silong, the space under the raised floor of a bahay kubo, mainly used for?
o: A children's playroom with a bamboo roof
Storing tools, firewood, and keeping small livestock
questions.ref: Diksyonaryong Biswal term list cited in the supplied recall; common Filipino vernacular-architecture usage
questions.n: The silong is the shaded under-floor space. Word root: silong comes from the idea of taking shelter (sumilong = to take shelter). Think of it as the house's built-in garage and storeroom.

questions.q: Which architect designed the Bauhaus building in Dessau?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: Gropius founded the Bauhaus and designed the Dessau school (1925-26). Word root: German Bau (building) + Haus (house).

questions.q: Plants grown on stacked shelves or racks to save floor space are an example of what?
questions.ref: UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); urban-agriculture terminology
questions.n: Grow up, not out. Think of a bookshelf where each shelf is a garden.

questions.q: Which Roman structure is semicircular and used for plays and entertainment?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on ancient Roman building types
questions.n: Word root: Greek theatron from theasthai, 'to behold'. A theater is half of an amphitheater. A circus was for chariot races.

questions.q: Plants grown in pots, containers, or grow bags are an example of what?
questions.ref: UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); urban-agriculture terminology
questions.n: The container is the mini-garden bed. Easy for balconies and rooftops.

questions.q: A specification that states only the required end result is called what?
questions.ref: Standard construction-specification practice (CSI-style spec types)
questions.n: You say what it must do, not how. Think of 'make it waterproof' versus 'use this exact membrane'.

questions.q: What is the recommended basic fee (RBF) for architectural and engineering services?
questions.ref: UAP Doc 202 (Design Services), schedule of minimum basic fees and payment phases
questions.n: PCC is under P50M, so the 7% rate applies to the whole cost.

questions.q: What material was the Ziggurat of Ur mainly built from?
questions.ref: General references on Mesopotamian architecture; Ziggurat of Ur (Ur-Nammu)
questions.n: A mud-brick core with a baked-brick skin. Mesopotamia had clay, not stone. Think of a giant layer cake: soft inside, hard crust outside.

questions.q: Which system grows plants using nutrient-rich water from fish tanks?
questions.ref: UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); urban-agriculture terminology
questions.n: Fish waste feeds plants, plants clean the water. Word root: Latin aqua (water) + Greek ponos (labor).

questions.q: A specification that names a specific brand or product is called what?
questions.ref: Standard construction-specification practice (CSI-style spec types)
questions.n: Word root: proprietary from Latin proprius, 'one's own', meaning owned by a brand. Think of ordering 'a Coke' instead of 'a cola'.

questions.q: Which style did Frank Lloyd Wright establish, known for low horizontal lines inspired by the Midwest landscape?
questions.ref: General references on Frank Lloyd Wright's life and works
questions.n: Long low roofs echo the flat prairie horizon.

questions.q: Which soil-free system grows plants with roots hanging in air and sprayed with a nutrient mist?
questions.ref: UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); urban-agriculture terminology
questions.n: Word root: Greek aer (air) + ponos (labor). Roots in the air.

questions.q: What is the main characteristic of the Ziggurat of Ur?
questions.ref: General references on Mesopotamian architecture; Ziggurat of Ur (Ur-Nammu)
questions.n: Stacked, shrinking platforms like a wedding cake. A true pyramid has smooth sloped sides.

questions.q: Using or occupying a building without the appropriate Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation is which class of violation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Memory ladder: not posting a certificate (light) < using without one (less grave) < changing use without one (grave). Less grave = P8,000 fine.

questions.q: What architectural style is the Bauhaus Dessau building?
questions.ref: General references on the Bauhaus Dessau building (Walter Gropius, 1925-26)
questions.n: Flat roofs, glass, steel, and no ornament are hallmarks of the International Style.

questions.q: An ASEAN architect from abroad works on a Philippine project with a local architect. How is the foreign practitioner classified?
questions.ref: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR, definitions of Architect-of-Record, AICC, Consulting Architect, Foreign Architect
questions.n: A foreign architect holding a permit cannot be the AOR. The Filipino counterpart must serve as AOR.

questions.q: A layout that is easy to understand regardless of language or experience, even without text signs, follows which principle?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: A good door explains itself: push plate means push. Color-coded zones that guide people without words also help here.

questions.q: What is the central debate between heritage preservation and modernization?
o: Whether stone or wood is stronger
Which building is cheaper to paint
Keeping historic character versus updating for modern needs and use
questions.ref: General heritage-conservation practice (Intramuros / Casa Manila context)
questions.n: The tension is authenticity versus function.

questions.q: Unauthorized change in construction type from more fire-resistive to less fire-resistive is which class of violation?
questions.ref: PD 1096 Revised IRR, Rule II, Sec. 212 (Administrative Fines)
questions.n: Weakening a building's fire resistance risks lives, so it is graded grave.

questions.q: Which school did Frank Lloyd Wright establish?
questions.ref: General references on Frank Lloyd Wright's life and works
questions.n: An apprenticeship community started in 1932. Word root: Taliesin is Welsh for 'shining brow', named for the hillside site.

questions.q: What type of building is Arthaland Century Pacific Tower?
questions.ref: Public project descriptions by Arthaland, GFP Architects, and the IFC EDGE / World GBC case study
questions.n: It is a premium-grade office tower in Bonifacio Global City.

questions.q: What are the usual window characteristics of Romanesque buildings?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on Romanesque architecture
questions.n: Thick masonry walls carry the heavy roof, so big windows would weaken them. Think of a castle wall: strong but with only small slits.

questions.q: What is the basis of the ziggurat's orientation?
questions.ref: General references on Mesopotamian architecture; Ziggurat of Ur (Ur-Nammu)
questions.n: The structure is aligned to the cardinal points, a sign of deliberate religious planning.

questions.q: Which Roman structure has seating all around an arena and was used for gladiator fights?
questions.ref: General architectural-history references on ancient Roman building types
questions.n: Word root: Greek amphi (on both sides, around) + theatron (viewing place). Two theaters glued together makes a full oval.

questions.q: A space that can easily adapt to many uses or users follows which principle?
questions.ref: Center for Universal Design (NC State), Principles of Universal Design
questions.n: Think of a Swiss army knife: one design, many uses.

questions.q: Who is the architect of record of Arthaland Century Pacific Tower?
questions.ref: Public project descriptions by Arthaland, GFP Architects, and the IFC EDGE / World GBC case study
questions.n: GFP is the Filipino architect of record. SOM of New York did the design in collaboration. Remember: the architect of record signs and seals local documents.

questions.q: Casa Manila in Intramuros was built as a replica of a 19th-century Spanish-colonial house. Which conservation term best describes it?
questions.ref: General heritage-conservation practice (Intramuros / Casa Manila context)
questions.n: Reconstruction means building it again from records, while restoration repairs original fabric. Casa Manila is a museum-house, so 'Re-' plus 'construct' fits.

questions.q: Which part is the open or lightly covered area beside the kitchen used for washing, laundry, and similar wet chores?
questions.ref: Diksyonaryong Biswal term list cited in the supplied recall; common Filipino vernacular-architecture usage
questions.n: The batalan is the house's outdoor wet area. Think of it as a veranda that works as the laundry and washing station, kept open so water drains away.

questions.q: What type of glazing is used on the tower's facade?
questions.ref: Public project descriptions by Arthaland, GFP Architects, and the IFC EDGE / World GBC case study
questions.n: Two glass layers trap an insulating air gap, like a thermos for the building.
